players.product: EPCM lead / general contractor for AI data-center campuses (Hut 8 River Bend and Beacon Point)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 revenue (CFO Venk Nathamuni): gross revenue increased more than 34% year over year and adjusted net revenue, which excludes pass-through revenue, grew by over 8% (CEO Bob Pragada: more than 8% adjusted net revenue growth, all organic).
quarterly_data.figure: gross revenue >+34%; adjusted net revenue >+8% (all organic)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 profitability (CEO Bob Pragada / CFO Venk Nathamuni): adjusted EPS grew approximately 14% to $1.84 - the sixth straight quarter of double-digit adjusted EPS growth; adjusted EBITDA was $367 million, up 17%, at a 15.2% margin (109 basis points higher year over year).
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS $1.84 (~+14%); adjusted EBITDA $367 million (+17%), margin 15.2% (+109 bps)

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog grew 27% to a record $29 billion, with a trailing 12-month book-to-bill of 1.4x on gross revenue and 1.2x on net revenue; net revenue and gross profit in backlog increased 11% and 14% year over year. Awards stood out in advanced manufacturing, environmental and transportation; CEO: net-revenue book-to-bill of about 1.1x to 1.3x is pretty consistent, while gross book-to-bill is lumpier as large full program delivery jobs are booked.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $29 billion (+27%); TTM book-to-bill 1.4x gross, 1.2x net; net revenue in backlog +11%, gross profit in backlog +14%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 outlook raised for the third consecutive time (CFO Venk Nathamuni): adjusted net revenue growth 9.5%-10%, adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 14.7%-14.8%, adjusted EPS $7.20-$7.30 (nearly 19% growth at the midpoint), adjusted free cash flow margin 8%. Q4: adjusted EBITDA margin approximately 16%, net revenue growth approximately 14% (the extra week in Q4 accounts for about 6%-7%), tax rate roughly 27.5%, free cash flow approximately $150 million. FY2027: growth at least in line with the long-term average, with specifics on the next call.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted net revenue growth 9.5%-10%; adjusted EBITDA margin 14.7%-14.8%; adjusted EPS $7.20-$7.30; FCF margin 8%; Q4 margin ~16%, net revenue growth ~14%

quarterly_data.signal: AI build-out (management): the direct AI build-out represented 11% of adjusted net revenue as of Q3, up approximately 100 basis points from last quarter (roughly 10%), and the growth is accelerating. CEO: data center backlog growth has been significant - 'I'd say in the order of doubling over the period of time' - the pipeline has gone up 3x and visibility now extends two to three years (vs six to nine months before); Jacobs is selective because there is a lot of speculative work and wins with established customers - the neocloud providers that are coming in are normally backed by folks Jacobs has known for a long time within the hyperscaler world. CFO: 'we expect significant growth in fiscal 2027' from AI, to be quantified.
quarterly_data.figure: direct AI build-out 11% of adjusted net revenue (~+100 bps QoQ); data center pipeline up 3x

quarterly_data.signal: Life sciences and advanced manufacturing net revenue grew 24% in Q3, the highest growth rate since Jacobs began reporting end markets in late 2024, driven by strong data center and semiconductor performance, a trend the CFO anticipates will continue in Q4. CEO Bob Pragada, asked whether the sector can grow double digits for the foreseeable future: 'we absolutely can' - from high-bandwidth memory chip work to the water and power requirements feeding the data center, Jacobs' share is increasing.
quarterly_data.figure: life sciences and advanced manufacturing net revenue +24%

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductors (CEO Bob Pragada): customers are pushing Jacobs to accelerate U.S. semiconductor designs; Jacobs is working for the largest high bandwidth memory chip manufacturer in the U.S. today and has been the engineer of record for Intel for a couple of decades, with the Intel pipeline starting to grow going into 2027. Jacobs is a leading facility designer for the semiconductor industry, whose capacity needs are rising with the AI data center build-out.

CEO Bob Pragada on 800 V data centers: the 800 V DC solid-state transformer 'is a big deal', but not the single source of the inflection - the complexity of utility requirements to feed the next generation of chips is increasing complexity and scale, which is Jacobs' sweet spot; it works with hyperscalers and neoclouds. Jacobs' services now range from technical advisory and design to digital twins and full program delivery.

Segments: Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities posted nearly $2.1 billion of net revenue, up 10% and a quarterly record, with operating profit up 14%. PA Consulting operating profit rose 2% on flattish revenue with operating margin above 22%; PA saw temporary disruption from the change in U.K. government leadership (delayed project starts), already returning to normal, with solid quarter-on-quarter growth forecast for Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: I&AF net revenue nearly $2.1 billion (+10%), operating profit +14%; PA operating profit +2%, margin above 22%

quarterly_data.signal: Critical infrastructure net revenue increased 9% year over year, led by transportation (high single-digit growth: aviation, rail, ports and maritime, highways and bridges) and energy and power (double-digit growth, mainly U.S. T&D work and, outside the U.S., generation such as SuedLink and Marinus Link); Jacobs expects mid-to-high single-digit growth over the medium term. The Middle East saw a temporary pause but still grew on utility work; international growth is about 9% (Europe stable, mid-single digits).
quarterly_data.figure: critical infrastructure net revenue +9%; international ~9% growth

quarterly_data.signal: Water and environmental net revenue grew a little more than 1% (water still high single-digit, environmental facing headwinds); two sizable private-sector industrial environmental wins (clients not named) took the environmental book-to-bill over 1.3x, and management forecasts sequential improvement in Q4 and CEO says Jacobs is positioned extremely well to be at the investor-day mid-to-high single-digit growth rates for water and environmental in FY2027. Q3 awards included program management and technical environmental services for the U.S. Navy's Environmental Restoration Program (Mid-Atlantic and Puerto Rico) and Central Utah Water Conservancy District's Strawberry High Line Improvement Project (roughly 40 mi of canal), part of the approximately $1.5 billion Nebo Regional Water Project.
quarterly_data.figure: water and environmental net revenue a little more than 1%; environmental book-to-bill over 1.3x; ~40 mi canal; ~$1.5 billion Nebo program

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Venk Nathamuni: Q3 adjusted free cash flow was $541 million (excluding payments related to the PA transaction), $633 million year to date; margins went from 13.4% to 14.1% to 15.2% over the last three quarters. FY2025 margins rose 110 basis points and the FY2026 guidance midpoint adds another 90 basis points, driven by operating leverage and global delivery; CEO expects FY2027 margin expansion from both I&AF and PA Consulting.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted FCF $541 million (Q3), $633 million YTD; margins 13.4% / 14.1% / 15.2%

connects_to.relationship: EPCM / general contractor for River Bend and Beacon Point

contracts.signal: CEO Bob Pragada: in Q3 Jacobs was awarded a sole-source EPCM contract by Hut 8 to deliver Beacon Point, its second AI data center campus in the U.S. (Texas, multi-phase, designed to support 1 GW of total capacity), a follow-on to Hut 8's River Bend campus in Louisiana where Jacobs is also leading program delivery; Jacobs will reuse River Bend design elements and deploy its data center digital twin, with initial energization targeted for 2027.
